config.overviewNewFeatureBulkUndoHow: The toast now offers Undo for eight seconds and puts every bookmark back in the position it held. A delete that fails puts them back on its own and says so. The trash still catches everything for 30 days after that.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarksMenuHow: Right-click any row for one menu on that row: open it, copy the address, edit, move it to another page or category, change how often it is checked, pin it, or delete it. Right-click a row that is part of a selection and the menu switches to the whole selection, with the count named.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkSettingsHow: Ten settings of its own, including what a quick-added bookmark starts with, the interval a bookmark gets when you switch it to Monitor, how many rows a delete has to touch before it asks, what counts as "not opened in a while", and which archive service the archive links point at.
config.overviewNewFeatureUsageDataHow: Search takes added: and opened: with today, week, month or year — and opened:never. Your own collections can now use pinned, untagged, days since last opened and days since last changed, and a Recently added collection answers the one question the others never could.
config.overviewNewFeatureRowKeysHow: Shift + P pins, Shift + S shares, Shift + R opens the row in Health, and t filters to its tag. Ctrl/Cmd + Enter opens a bookmark in a new tab for that press alone, whatever your standing preference says. Pin also has a right-click entry now.
config.overviewNewFeatureRowTagsHow: Switch on tags in the grid and the first two appear on the row, with the rest collapsing into a count. They give way before the bookmark name does, and stay out of the way on a phone.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxTagsHow: Tags now sit on the row. Click one to see only that tag, and click it again to go back. Right-click a link and choose Tags to edit them, search matches them along with the title and note, and both the CSV and JSON exports carry them.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxStatsHow: The Stats button in the Inbox toolbar shows how many links you have added, promoted and deleted, what share of the ones you decided on became bookmarks, and how long a link sits there before you deal with it.
config.overviewNewFeatureSpacingHow: Config → Appearance → Layout now has Category spacing and Page margins, each with Snug, Balanced and Airy.
config.overviewNewFeatureStructureTrashHow: Both now go to the trash for 30 days. A page is one entry — listed as “Page · 12 bookmarks” — and restoring brings the page, its categories and its bookmarks back in a single action.
config.overviewNewFeatureCategoryGridHow: A + sits beside the A–Z / Rec chips in a category header, and holding c does the same from the keyboard. Both act on the page on screen, so neither asks which page you meant.
config.overviewNewFeaturePageOverviewHow: Press , for the overview and use the New page row under the list — by click, by n, or by arrowing one stop past the last page.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthBulkHow: Tick the box on any row, or press x to tick the one under the cursor and move on, X for everything the filter shows. A bar appears above the list with Set checking, Re-check, Open, Copy links and Delete.
config.overviewNewFeatureBulkTagsHow: Select some rows and press the toolbar’s Tags button. Every tag you already use is listed, with a tick when the whole selection has it and “on 2 of 3” when only some do.
config.overviewNewFeatureFormCreateHow: Both dropdowns in the bookmark form lead with ➕ New page… and ➕ New category…. Picking one swaps the dropdown for a name box, and the new page or category is selected when you come back.
config.overviewNewFeatureMultiSelectHow: Press x to tick the row under the cursor, X for the whole category, Shift+↑/↓ for a range, Ctrl/Cmd+A for everything on screen — or Alt+click and Shift+click with the mouse. Select is in the right-click menu too.
config.overviewNewFeatureTrashHow: Restore puts a bookmark back on its own page at its old position. Delete forever and Empty trash clear it early.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthContextMenuHow: Right-click any row in the Health view to open that same menu at the cursor, the way a bookmark on the dashboard already did. Shift and right-click still gives you the browser’s own menu.
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitorEmphasisHow: Right-click a bookmark and pick Show in Health to jump straight to its row, from the dashboard or from Config → Bookmarks.
config.overviewNewFeatureSideRailHow: Pick a position under Config → Appearance → Button bar, or run :buttonbar from the command palette. The bar moves as you choose — no reload.
config.overviewNewFeatureNewsStreamHow: The chips above the list narrow it to one source, or hide the site's posts entirely. A green dot marks what arrived since you last read it, and All news & features opens the whole list under About.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardHow: Hover a bookmark. Shift + V keeps the card open with Copy, Refresh and Edit, and Esc closes it. A line with nothing to say is left out, so a bare link is a short card rather than empty space.
config.overviewNewFeatureButtonBarTabHow: Appearance → Button bar holds both halves: the five positions, each drawn as the page with the bar in it, and under them the main buttons and the extras with Show all, Hide all and a count. Toolbar & tabs keeps the header row, which is a different strip.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkFormHow: Press +, Shift+B, or Ctrl+Shift+A to open the form. Use Create + New to save and immediately add another; the grid updates behind the modal.
config.overviewNewFeatureUpdateCheckHow: Press Check for updates in the ★ modal header or on Config → Overview. When a newer release exists, open GitHub from the notice or dismiss it until the next version.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarksFiltersHow: Type in the search box (shortcuts match too), pick page or category from the dropdowns, or click a page, category, or tag on a row. Sort by last opened, most opened, or pinned first. Tick rows for bulk favicon refresh or CSV export.
config.overviewNewFeaturePagesTagsTabsHow: Use [ and ] to cycle sub-tabs from anywhere in config, or click Categories or Tags in the strip. Pages, Finders, and Collections follow after.
config.overviewNewFeatureRandomThemeHow: Choose Off (always your saved theme), On page refresh (new pick on each reload), or On view change (new pick when switching between bookmarks, config, inbox, health, or dashboard pages). With auto dark mode, only matching light or dark variants are eligible. While random is on, a Currently showing hint names the active theme.
config.overviewAboutBody: Hi, I’m Jordi, a developer from the Netherlands. I build nextDash in my spare time, scratching my own itch: a bookmark dashboard that is fast, keyboard-first, and stores everything in plain files you own. It is free and open-source, and it stays that way. If it saves you time too, a star on GitHub or a coffee is always appreciated — and bug reports and ideas are just as welcome.
config.overviewAboutBodyShort: Hi, I’m Jordi, a developer from the Netherlands. I build nextDash in my spare time: a bookmark dashboard that is fast, keyboard-first, and stores everything in plain files you own. Free and open-source, and it stays that way.
config.whatsNewUnavailable: Could not open the release notes.
config.helpFindersBody:
Finders are search shortcuts that send a query straight to an external site instead of searching your bookmarks. ?g nextdash searches Google for “nextdash”; ?w might go to Wikipedia. Open finder mode with ? or from the toolbar, and a fresh install starts with DuckDuckGo on du.

The point is the round trip you skip: no loading the site, finding its search box, then typing. One prefix and your text goes where it was always going.

Defining your own under Pages & tags → Finders takes three things: a shortcut, a display name, and a URL with %s where the query belongs. To get the URL, run any search on the site and copy the address, then replace what you searched for with %s:

  • Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=%s
  • GitHub — https://github.com/search?q=%s
  • Your own docs, an internal wiki, a ticket tracker — anything with a search URL works, including sites only reachable on your own network.

Multi-word queries are encoded for you, so ?w keyboard layout behaves as typing it into the site itself would. Leave the query off entirely — just ?w — and you land on the site’s own search page.

Names and shortcuts have to be unique. Two finders answering to ?g would leave which one runs down to chance, so a duplicate is refused as you type it rather than accepted and quietly ignored later.

Tags can be attached to a finder, which keeps a long list navigable once you have more than a handful. nextDash also counts how often each is used, so the ones you actually reach for rise to the top of the list.

Blending them into ordinary search. Turn on Include finders in search under Behavior → Search and finders appear alongside bookmarks in normal > results — so one keystroke can reach either, without deciding up front whether you are looking for something you saved or something you want to look up.
config.helpCommandsBody:
: opens the command palette — actions rather than destinations. A lone : lists everything grouped by area, with the commands you use most floating to the top, so the palette gets shorter as it learns what you reach for. Type to narrow, Enter to run.

Many commands take an argument and complete as you type, so you rarely have to remember exact wording — :op is enough to be offered the :open … family. The space between a command and its argument is a space: it used to run the highlighted row instead, so a command taking an argument could not be finished by typing.

Opening several at once. These open real browser tabs, so a large selection opens a lot of them:

  • :open last 5 — reopen what you opened most recently. 3, 5 and 10 are offered; any number works.
  • :open tag work · :open category news — everything carrying a tag, or in a category
  • :open pinned — every pinned bookmark
  • :open all — everything on the current page. Worth a glance at the count first.

Finding and filtering without leaving the palette:

  • :tag work — list bookmarks with a tag in the palette, dashboard untouched
  • :filter / :filter clear — apply or drop a dashboard tag filter
  • :find / :find clear — the same for a text filter
  • :recent · :saved · :history — what you opened lately, and what you kept
  • :duplicates · :stale 30 — the two cleanup lists, without opening health

Changing how it looks, which is quicker than opening config and easy to undo:

  • :theme · :dark — switch theme or force dark
  • :layout modern · :density compact · :columns 4 — try a look without committing to it
  • :sort — change the sort mode of the focused category
  • :preview · :animations · :opacity — toggle the smaller visual settings

Housekeeping and getting somewhere:

  • :favicons fetch — re-download every bookmark’s icon
  • :backup · :export — open backups, or download an export straight away
  • :health refresh · :health broken — re-check availability, or jump to what is broken
  • :inbox · :inbox triage — open the inbox, or start working through it
  • :page new · :category new — create one without a trip to config
  • :goto config · :goto health · :goto stats — jump straight to a view
  • :note — edit a bookmark’s note in place
  • :cheat · :help · :whatsnew — the cheat sheet, this guide, or the release notes

The palette is the fastest way to reach anything you do occasionally, but not often enough to remember where it lives.
config.packagedThemesNote: Recolour a theme that ships with nextDash, or the base light and dark palettes. Reset defaults puts a packaged theme back to how it shipped.
config.themeResetConfirm: Reset the packaged themes to their original colours? Your own themes are kept.
config.generalGroupOnboardingNote: The quick-start card, the occasional keyboard tip, and the release summary.
config.generalGroupHyprModeNote: For nextDash installed as a Progressive Web App (PWA). Clicking a bookmark opens it in a new browser tab, then closes the PWA window automatically — the behaviour of a traditional app launcher.
config.statsInboxIntro: What is waiting in the inbox, and how much of it you turn into bookmarks.
config.customCollectionsNote: Group bookmarks by rules on their tags, category or shortcut. They appear on the dashboard alongside the smart collections.
config.collectionNameDuplicate: A collection with this name already exists.
config.collectionNoRules: Add a rule to match bookmarks.
config.resetIntro: These actions permanently remove data. Make a backup first — there is no undo.
config.resetTypePrompt: Type {token} to confirm this permanent reset:
config.resetTypeMismatch: That does not match — nothing was changed.
config.resetTypeNote: You will be asked to type {token} to confirm.
config.statsConcentrationBody: Your top {top} bookmarks account for {share}% of all {total} opens.
config.statsConcentrationRest: The other {n} used bookmarks share the remaining {pct}%.
config.statsCategoryEffNote: How often a bookmark in this category gets opened. A low figure on a large category is one you built but do not use.
config.statsCleanupNote: Each opens the matching bookmarks, where they can be tagged or removed in bulk.
config.statsCleanupNoIconHint: Falls back to a letter tile
config.cleanupFilterChangedHint: Bookmarks added or edited in the last seven days
config.healthRecheckIntervalInfoMessage:
How long the server waits between background health re-checks.

• 15 minutes to 24 hours
• Only applies while background rechecks are switched on
• Longer intervals make fewer outbound requests
config.monitorNotifyRetriesInfoMessage:
How many checks in a row must fail before an alert is sent.

• Default: 3
• Higher values ride out brief blips without alerting
• 1 alerts on the very first failed check
config.smartTodayLimitInfoMessage:
How many bookmarks the Today collection shows at most.

• Unlimited shows every match
• Only affects the display; nothing is removed
config.smartRecentLimitInfoMessage:
How many bookmarks the Recently opened collection shows at most.

• Unlimited shows every match
• Only affects the display; nothing is removed
config.smartStaleLimitInfoMessage:
How many bookmarks the Stale collection shows at most.

• Unlimited shows every match
• Only affects the display; nothing is removed
config.smartMostUsedLimitInfoMessage:
How many bookmarks the Most used collection shows at most.

• Unlimited shows every match
• Only affects the display; nothing is removed
config.bookmarksPageFilterPromoBody: Pick a page to see only its bookmarks and categories. The address bar becomes a link you can share (#config/bookmarks/…).
config.overviewNewFeatureKeyboardHow: Use j/k or arrow keys on the section rail, [ and ] for sub-tabs, and list keys on Pages & tags and Bookmarks. Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+K opens Find settings.
config.overviewNewFeatureFindSettingsHow: Press Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+K anywhere in config, or click Find settings below Help in the left nav. Type to filter, then Enter to go.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkPagesHow: Choose a page in the filter dropdown to scope categories and deep-link with #config/bookmarks/<pageId>. With All pages, categories show as Page · Category.
config.appearanceDisplayQuickNote: Everyday bookmark row options. Toolbar and tab visibility live on their own tab.
config.tipAddAnywhere: Shift+B opens the new-bookmark form from anywhere on the dashboard, even while something else has focus.
config.tipAddCapture: Install nextDash as an app and it appears in your phone's share sheet; on a desktop browser the bookmarklet under Help → Inbox saves the page you are looking at.
config.tipAddDuplicate: Saving a link you already have on another page tells you where it is and offers to open it — Save anyway keeps the second copy when you meant it.
config.cheatsheetPdfHint: Every keyboard shortcut, ready to print (opens in a new tab)
config.bookmarksTagCloudHint: Filter by one or more tags
config.shortcutTooltipsLabel: Show shortcut hints on toolbar icons
config.shortcutTooltipsInfoMessage:
When enabled, hovering a header link or toolbar button shows its name and keyboard shortcut.

• Helps you learn the keys
• Turn off for a quieter dashboard

Also available as :shortcuts on|off in the command panel.
config.statsAxisShareHealthy: Healthy share of {total} tracked bookmarks — 0% to 100%
config.statsActivityLifetimeHint: Counted over the whole life of these bookmarks, not only this period — nextDash stores a total per bookmark, not a date for every open.
config.statsActivityNote: Each bar counts the bookmarks whose last use falls in that period. A bookmark appears once, on the day you last opened it.
config.statsEmptyBody: Statistics fill in as you add bookmarks and start opening them. Add a few and this page will have something to say.
config.statsConcentrationEmpty: Nothing has been opened yet, so there is no usage to weigh up.
config.statsInboxTrendNote: What arrived against what you dealt with. Recorded per day as it happened, so this is real history rather than a snapshot.
config.statsInboxTrendEmpty: No inbox activity in this period.
config.statsHeadlineShortcuts: You reach for bookmarks by keystroke: {pct}% carry a shortcut, against {tagPct}% carrying tags.
config.statsHeadlineTags: You organise by tag: {pct}% of bookmarks carry one, against {shortcutPct}% carrying a shortcut.
config.statsHeadlineNarrow: A narrow habit on a broad collection: your busiest {top} bookmarks account for {share}% of all opens.
config.statsHeadlineBroad: Your usage is spread out: {used} of {total} bookmarks have been opened, with no small group dominating.
config.statsHeadlineUnused: Nothing has been opened yet, so there is no habit to read from this collection.
config.logsIntro: What the server has been doing. Lines are kept in memory and in a rotating file, and mirrored to the container log as before.
config.logCaptureHint: Off by default. While this is off nothing is collected and the log costs nothing; what has already been collected is kept.
config.logEmptyStopped: Not collecting. Switch on Collect server log above to start.
config.logRetentionHintCount: Only the newest entries are kept; older ones drop off as new lines arrive. Age is not considered in this mode.
config.logRetentionHint: Older lines are dropped automatically. The newest lines are always kept, whatever the age limit.
config.logDetailHint: What the server writes at all — to this log and to the container log (docker logs). Takes effect immediately, on the very next line: no restart, and nothing to change in your compose file. What is not written costs nothing.
config.logDetailLiveQuiet: docker logs is now showing problems only, from the next line onwards.
config.logDetailLiveNormal: docker logs is now showing what the server does, from the next line onwards.
config.logDetailLiveVerbose: docker logs is now showing every step, from the next line onwards.
config.logChannelsResetTitle: Record the two channels nextDash records by default
config.logFloorQuiet: Recording at Quiet — only problems are kept, so this list will be short.
config.logFloorNormal: Recording at Normal — debug lines are not kept.
config.logFloorVerbose: Recording at Verbose — every step is kept.
config.logChannelsHint: A machine-readable record of what happened, kept apart from the readable lines above. Pick what belongs in it.
config.logClearConfirm: Delete every stored log line? The file on disk goes too, and this cannot be undone.
config.logLoadFailed: Could not read the server log.
config.trashIntro: Deleted bookmarks, pages and categories stay here for {days} days, then go for good.
config.trashRestorePageIdTaken: A different page now uses that page’s slot, so it cannot be restored without replacing it.
config.trashRestorePageGone: That bookmark’s page no longer exists. It stays in the trash — recreate the page, then restore it.
config.trashEmptyConfirm: Permanently delete everything in the trash?
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitoringHow: Press c on a row in Health and choose Monitor. The server then checks it on its own interval, whether or not you have the dashboard open, and the row grows a heartbeat, an uptime percentage and an outage history. Say what "up" means for that page with a keyword or specific status codes, watch for it quietly turning into a different page, and get an alert on Slack, Telegram, Pushover and others when it goes down.
config.overviewNewFeatureWorkThroughHow: Open Health and press f, or use the Work through button. One bookmark fills the screen with its actions large — re-check, open, delete, skip — and j and k move between them. Esc leaves you on the row you had reached, so dipping in for three fixes and back out is not a mode switch.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemePreviewHow: Open the Theme list under Appearance and move through it: the dashboard behind takes on each theme as you go. Press Esc or click away and you are back where you started. There are 23 new themes to look through as well.
config.overviewNewFeatureSettingsSearchHow: Every setting is searchable the moment you open Config, and settings answer to more than their exact label — “uptime”, “wallpaper” and “hotkey” each find the right one even though those words are nowhere on screen.
config.overviewNewFeatureChangedSettingsHow: At a glance now says how many settings differ from the standard and takes you to them. Each tab of settings gained Only changed, and each group a Reset panel that puts the whole lot back at once.
config.overviewNewFeatureToolbarGroupsHow: The header strip keeps its group under Toolbar & tabs; the two halves of the button bar sit on the Button bar tab, under the control that says where the bar goes. Each group has Show all and Hide all with a count of what is showing.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxExplainHow: Every count now means what you can act on right now, every pill carries its own, and a sentence under the toolbar says what the active filter selects. The ℹ beside Triage covers snoozing, promoting and the rest.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthStatsHow: The Monitored filter now opens with pooled uptime across every monitor, the least available ones, anything slower than last week, and every outage. The header draws the share of healthy bookmarks over the last 90 days.
config.ptViewOnlySorted: View only — the saved order is unchanged. Clear the sort to move rows again.
config.ptViewOnlyFiltered: View only — clear the search to move rows again.
config.maintenanceNote: Times when downtime is expected — a nightly backup, a weekly reboot. Checks still run and the heartbeat still records what happened, but failures inside a window raise no alert and do not count against uptime.
config.maintenanceEmpty: No windows. Alerts fire whenever a monitored bookmark goes down.
config.maintenanceIncomplete: Set a start and end time — an incomplete window is ignored.
config.maintenanceSameTime: Start and end are the same, so this window covers nothing and is ignored.
config.maintenanceWraps: Runs past midnight into the next day.
config.findersLoadFailed: Finders could not be loaded, so they will not be saved. Reload and try again.
config.categoriesLoadFailed: Categories could not be loaded, so they will not be saved. Reload and try again.
config.collectionsDropped: Not saved: {names}. A collection needs a name and at least one rule with a value.
config.nameTooLong: That name is too long (max {max} characters).
config.themeImportError: That file is not a nextDash theme.
config.csvImportError: Could not read that CSV file.
config.csvImportEmpty: No bookmarks found in that file.
config.csvImportConfirm: Import {n} bookmarks onto the current page?
config.trashRestoredSomeFailed: Restored {ok}. {failed} could not be restored and stay in the trash.
config.trashLoadFailed: The trash could not be loaded.
config.bookmarksGroupListNote: How this list opens and how much of it loads at a time.
config.bookmarksGroupNewNote: What a bookmark added with & or + starts out as.
config.bookmarksGroupBulkNote: When to ask first, and what counts as neglected.
config.bulkFaviconConfirm: Fetch icons for {n} bookmarks? This can take a while.
config.configBookmarksSortInfoMessage: The order this list is in when you open it. Health and the Inbox remember their sort; this one used to start on page order every time.
config.configBookmarksPageSizeInfoMessage: How many rows are added each time you reach the end of the list. Lower is lighter on a phone; higher gives more overview during a clean-up.
config.bookmarkDeleteConfirmFromInfoMessage: Deleting this many rows or more asks first. Set it higher to work through a clean-up without a dialog each time — every delete still offers an undo and stays in the trash for 30 days.
config.defaultMonitorIntervalInfoMessage: The interval a bookmark gets when you switch it to Monitor without choosing one, including in bulk.
config.newBookmarkCheckModeInfoMessage: What a quick-added bookmark starts on. Useful if you run services and want each one checked from the moment you add it.
config.newBookmarkPinnedInfoMessage: Whether a quick-added bookmark is pinned to the top of its category straight away.
config.bookmarkStaleDaysInfoTitle: When a bookmark counts as neglected
config.bookmarkStaleDaysInfoMessage: Used by the statistics and by the clean-up score that tells you a page needs attention. A daily work library is neglected sooner than a reference archive.
config.bulkFaviconConfirmFromInfoTitle: When to confirm an icon refresh
config.bulkFaviconConfirmFromInfoMessage: Fetching icons for this many selected rows asks first, the way the whole-dashboard refresh does. Zero never asks.
config.bookmarkArchiveUrlInfoMessage: Where "Find in Web Archive" sends a bookmark. {url} is replaced with its address, so a self-hosted ArchiveBox or archive.today works too.
config.showRowTagsInfoMessage: Adds a small chip per tag beside the bookmark name, the same chip the Inbox and Config → Bookmarks use. Off by default: a row with several tags is busier, and the grid earns its keep by staying scannable. Tags never push the name out — they give way first, and are hidden on a phone.
config.logActivityHint: What was done — bookmarks saved, pages added, checks run — mixed into the same log as the requests. Pick Activity only to read just those, or turn categories on and off with NEXTDASH_ACTIVITY_LOG.
config.statsNoActivityEver: Nothing has been opened yet, so there is nothing to plot. This fills in as you use your bookmarks.
config.statsScopeWholeLibrary: These figures cover the whole library, not just {page}.
config.statsHealthTrendWaiting: A day is recorded each time the health report runs. Once there are a few, the change over time appears here.
config.backupRotationNote: The newest {keep} are kept. Making another — or restoring, which copies the current data first — removes the oldest.
config.aboutFeatureCatalogue: Everything else you can switch on
config.aboutFeatureCatalogueNote: Settings from earlier releases, in the order they were written down.
config.aboutTrackTitle: Follow it from your own dashboard
config.aboutTrackNote: Save nextdash.cc as a bookmark and Fresh counts what it publishes, the same way it does for every other page you keep.
config.aboutTrackDone: nextdash.cc is already one of your bookmarks — Fresh will count new posts on it like any other page.
config.aboutTrackAdded: nextdash.cc is on your dashboard. Turn Fresh on under Behavior → Fresh to see what it publishes.
config.aboutIntro: What nextDash is, and where it comes from.
config.helpTipsIntro: Small things that save a keystroke, grouped by what you are doing. The dashboard shows one of these above the buttons when you switch that on.
config.helpCopyLink: Copy a link to this topic
config.helpLinkInAddressBar: The link is in the address bar.
config.sessionTipsInfoMessage:
A single shortcut hint rotates above the button bar, changing daily.

• On: one tip at a time, dismissible
• Off: nothing above the buttons

The full catalogue is in Config → Help → Tips either way.
config.monitorNotifyUrlInfoMessage:
The address the server posts to when a monitored bookmark goes down or comes back.

For a webhook this is the full URL your service gave you. For Pushover, leave it empty and fill in the two token fields instead.

The server posts from itself, so the address has to be reachable from where nextDash runs, not from your browser.
config.faviconRefreshPolicyInfoMessage:
How often a bookmark icon is re-downloaded from its site.

• Never: keep what is stored until you refresh by hand
• Monthly or Weekly: replace icons that have gone stale
• Every load: always current, and a request per bookmark per visit

Sites change their icons rarely, so Never or Monthly suits most collections.
config.usageAnalyticsInfoMessage:
Off unless you turn it on. When on, nextDash reports which features are used and roughly how large the collection is — every number rounded into a band, never bookmark names, addresses, searches or notes.

Switching it off stops the counting entirely rather than gathering and discarding it.
config.autoBackupInfoMessage:
A full backup on a schedule, kept in the data directory.

How often is up to you: daily, weekly, fortnightly or monthly. Only the newest few are kept, so making one on a full rotation drops the oldest.

Restoring or importing writes a copy of the current data first, so a restore you regret can itself be undone.

config.tipEverydayTyping: Just start typing on the dashboard: the letters go to the search line and the list narrows as you type. Enter opens the top result — nothing opens until you press it.
config.tipEverydayGridLetters: While a row is selected, letters belong to the grid: j/k move, x ticks, g starts a jump. Esc gives the letters back to the search line.
config.gridKeyLegendLabel: Show a key legend under the bookmarks
config.gridKeyLegendHint: Appears once you move the cursor with the keyboard and goes again when you open a bookmark. Press ! at any time for the full cheat sheet.
config.certWarnDaysInfoMessage:
Every HTTPS check completes a handshake anyway, so the expiry date costs nothing to read. This is how far ahead the first warning appears.

One number rather than three: two tighter marks follow it in the same proportion the built-in ladder uses — a month ahead also warns at a week and at three days, a fortnight ahead at three days and at one. A certificate belongs to a host, so ten bookmarks on one domain warn once and a single renewal clears them all.
config.rememberScrollPositionLabel: Come back to where you were on a page
config.rememberScrollPositionInfoTitle: Where you were on the page
config.rememberScrollPositionInfoMessage:
A long page is a place you are somewhere in, not a document you always read from the top. With this on, switching pages — or opening Health, Inbox or config and coming back — puts you back at the offset you left, and so does a reload, for as long as the browser tab is open.

A page that has since grown shorter simply clamps to its new end. Switch it off and every arrival lands at the top.
config.scopeThisDeviceHint: Kept in this browser, whichever way it is set.
config.scopeAllDevicesHint: Stays on the server even while settings are kept per device, so it is the same everywhere.

config.pageDuplicateBody: Copy this page, with its categories? You are asked about the bookmarks next.
config.pageDuplicateAskBookmarks: Copy the bookmarks too? Choosing no gives you the same categories, empty.

config.categoryDuplicateBookmarksFailed: The category was copied, but its bookmarks were not
config.helpCaptureTokenLabel: Capture token (only if this install has one)
config.helpCaptureTokenPlaceholder: leave empty when there is none
config.helpCaptureBookmarklet: Drag this to your bookmarks bar, or copy it
config.helpCaptureBody:
The browser extension covers Chrome and Chromium. Everywhere else — Safari, Firefox, a phone, a work laptop you cannot install anything on — there are two routes that need nothing installed. From a phone's share sheet. Install nextDash as an app (Add to Home Screen), and it appears in the share sheet of every app on the device. Sharing a link saves it to the inbox and opens nextDash on it. Android sometimes sends the address inside the text rather than as a link; nextDash picks it out either way. From any browser. The bookmarklet below saves the page you are looking at. Drag the button to your bookmarks bar, or copy the line and make a bookmark of it by hand. If this install has a write token, capture needs a token of its own: set NEXTDASH_CAPTURE_TOKEN on the server and paste it below. It opens nothing but these two routes, so a bookmarklet in someone else's browser history can at worst put a link in your inbox.

From a script, a launcher or a hotkey. The same route takes a plain GET /add?url=…&title=…, and the integrations/ folder in the repository carries ready-made pieces built on it: a shell script, two Raycast commands, a Dropzone action, a Ulauncher extension, and Alfred and Apple Shortcuts recipes.

config.widgetAuthQueryNote: This service takes its key in the address. It is kept in the credential file all the same, and put into the request as {name}.
config.widgetAuthSessionNote: nextDash signs in with these and keeps the session itself, so nothing has to be replaced when it expires.
config.widgetAuthRevealFailed: That key could not be read.
config.widgetAuthScheme: Most services want a scheme in front of the token here — "Bearer <token>" — not the token on its own.
config.widgetAuthNeedsPassword: Fill in the password as well.
config.widgetAuthNote: Kept in a separate file that stays out of your backups and exports, so a key never travels in a ZIP. The widget itself stores only a reference.
config.widgetsEmptyHint: A widget is a block beside your categories that holds something other than bookmarks.

config.statsUptimeHint: Pooled across every monitor by check, so a service checked often does not outweigh one checked rarely.
config.statsAxisUptime: Share of checks that succeeded — 0% to 100%
config.statsCertsHint: Only certificates near expiry are reported, one per host, and only for hosts reached over HTTPS. An empty panel means none are close.
config.statsArchiveHint: A dead link with a copy kept here is still readable. One without it is gone.
config.statsAxisShareArchived: Share of {total} bookmarks with a copy kept — 0% to 100%
config.statsLibraryHint: The rest of what this install holds — blocks on your pages, what feeds them, and what it keeps.
config.statsLibraryUnavailable: These figures could not be read.
config.helpWidgetKindsTitle: The kinds, and what each answers
config.helpWidgetKindsBody:
Nineteen built-in kinds, grouped in the picker under the question they answer.

Are the links still good? Health — how many bookmarks are broken, down, changed or fine, each figure opening its own filter. Uptime — the bookmarks you monitor, worst first, with uptime over the last week. Certificates — certificates about to expire, grouped by host rather than by bookmark, because ten bookmarks on one domain share one certificate. Health trend — broken links over time as a line, because the direction is what a single number cannot show.

What is arriving? Inbox — how much is waiting to be filed, and how long the oldest has waited. Feeds — feeds with new items, and the ones that stopped after repeated failures. Sources — what each import last did, so a failed import is not only visible inside config.

What needs tidying? Neglected — bookmarks you have not opened in a long time. Blind spots — never checked, checked long ago, or not watched at all. Duplicates — the same address stored more than once. Archive — how many bookmarks have a copy kept, and which broken ones have none. Trash — what is waiting there, and when retention removes it. Backups — how old the newest automatic backup is, and whether the last run failed.

How is this machine doing? Processor — how hard the CPU is working and the load average behind it, because either alone answers half the question: a load of 4 on four cores is a busy machine keeping up, while 30% with a load of 12 is one that is not. Memory — what is really in use, with the file cache counted as the spare room it is. Disks — free space on the disks you name, with used, free and reserved kept apart. Containers — how many run of how many exist, and which have a failing healthcheck. These four are the only widgets that read something outside nextDash, and the only ones that need setting up; see below.

What's happening around you? Weather — current conditions beside a forecast of three days, five days or the next 24 hours, for the location, source and unit already set under Behavior → Date & weather rather than asked for a second time. Calendar — what is coming up, from one ICS feed set for the whole install under Behavior → Date & weather → Calendar feed URL, with its own look-ahead in days and row count per widget. The server reads that feed rather than your browser, because the address a calendar app hands out is private and not meant for a script; a recurring event shows its own stated occurrence rather than every repeat.

And one more that is not a report but a capability: the Custom widget, below.
config.helpWidgetAddingTitle: Adding one, and where it sits
config.helpWidgetAddingBody:
Config → Widgets opens on the widgets you have, with one Add a widget button above them. The catalogue opens over the page rather than filling it — it used to sit open at the top of the tab, which pushed your own widgets below the fold, so choosing a kind added something you could not see. Now it closes onto the new widget with its name ready to type.

The Types tab is the same catalogue as reading matter: every kind with what it does, and an Add button on each, so you can read about one and take it without changing screens.

Finding one, once you have several. The tab carries the same toolbar as Bookmarks: a search, the page picker, a sort, and the button that adds something. Search matches the title and the type, because a widget you never named is drawn under its type — looking for “processor” and finding nothing on a page that plainly shows one is the kind of small lie a search should not tell. Sorting defaults to Grouped, under the same headings the catalogue uses, with Order on the page, Name A–Z and Type as the alternatives.

All pages in the page picker puts every page's widgets in one list, each row saying where it lives. It answers what have I actually got without visiting each page in turn — a widget on the page you are not looking at is the one you forget you are running. An edit made there is written back to the widget's own page. Adding is not offered while showing everything, since it has no answer to where.

Working on several at once. Tick any number of rows and a bar appears above them: Show, Hide, Move to page… and Delete. A move writes the destination first, so a failure leaves the widgets where they were rather than nowhere, and ids travel with them — a moved widget keeps the sign-in and the folded state filed under its id. Ticks are held by widget rather than by row position, so re-sorting cannot retarget them.

Settings per widget. Which page it counts, how many rows it shows, what it is called, how wide it is. Leave the title empty and it uses the kind's own name. An ℹ sits beside any setting that needs more than a line, and a ↺ clears every setting back to its default — offered only when something is actually off it, and written into the draft, so Save or Discard still decides. The title and the Shown switch are left alone by it: those are not settings with defaults, and quietly renaming a widget is not what a reset should mean.

Two changes save the moment you make them rather than waiting for Save: the title, and the Shown switch, which takes a widget off the dashboard without deleting it or losing its settings. Both say so when they land — a row with two ways of saving, one of them silent, is what made this tab feel like it might not have taken.

Where it sits is arranged under Pages & tags → categories, together with the categories it sits between — one order, one place to change it. On the dashboard you can also just drag it, the same as a category.
config.helpWidgetCustomBody:
Every widget above reads something nextDash already knows. The Custom widget reads a figure out of any service that answers with JSON, so a tile can show what your own machines are doing without waiting for nextDash to grow a widget for them. It is deliberately the only one that talks to anything outside.

An address that answers JSON. Any http or https endpoint. GET, or POST for the services that insist. It is fetched by the server, not by your browser — which is what makes a machine on your own network reachable at all, and what keeps a key out of a page any script could read. The address is stored rather than sent: the request names a widget, and the server visits only what that widget was already configured to visit.

Paths into the answer. Name the value you want and nothing else. A path walks objects and arrays — server.disk[0].used — and either names something or does not; a path that silently matched several things would make a wrong figure look right. Up to eight figures on one tile; more than that is a report rather than a glance.

A shape per figure. The same number reads differently depending on what it is: Count, Size, Percentage, Duration, Time ago, Text. Sizes step through KB and MB, a ratio between 0 and 1 is read as a percentage, and a date arrives as seconds, milliseconds or an ISO string.

Or a list instead of figures. Point at an array and the tile draws its entries as rows, up to twenty — the downloads running now, the last few errors.

A sign-in that stays out of your backups. An API key in a header, or a username and password. Credentials are named and reusable, shared with the health checks, and kept in a separate file that no export or backup ZIP includes; the widget itself stores only a reference to one.

Asked on a schedule you set. Anywhere between 30 seconds and a day, five minutes by default. One answer is shared by everyone looking at the dashboard, so a wall display costs the service nothing extra.

What it will not do is change anything. A tile reads, and the two methods it offers are the two that ask a question. An answer has eight seconds to arrive and is read up to a megabyte. There is no expression language and no arithmetic — the moment a config can compute, the config is a second product with its own bugs and no debugger.
config.helpWidgetServicesBody:
Twenty-eight services come filled in: pick one and the address, the figures worth reading and the header its API wants are already there. Everything stays editable afterwards, so a preset is a starting point rather than a lock.

Media & downloads. Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Readarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, Overseerr / Jellyseerr, Tautulli, Jellyfin / Emby, Plex, Immich, qBittorrent, SABnzbd, NZBGet.

Network. Pi-hole (v6 and v5 separately, because v6 rewrote its API), AdGuard Home, Traefik, Speedtest Tracker.

System. Proxmox VE, TrueNAS, Glances, Syncthing.

Apps. Nextcloud, Paperless-ngx, Home Assistant, Grafana, ntfy.

What a preset carries. A sample address in the right shape, so you can see what yours should look like; the path on that service that answers with the numbers worth a tile; the figures pulled out of it with their labels and shapes; and how it wants to be signed in to — an X-Api-Key header, a bearer token, a username and password, or nothing at all. Each names where to find its key: Sonarr's is under Settings → General, and the panel tells you so at the moment you need it.

A service that is not on this list needs no code — that is the whole point of the Custom widget. The presets exist because filling in an address, four paths and a header name from another program's documentation is the tedious half, not the hard half.
config.helpArtWidgetTrend: Or the direction it is going
config.helpArtWidgetFetched: Fetched here, never by your browser
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetFoldTitle: A widget folds away like the categories beside it
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetFoldWhat: A widget is a summary, and a page carrying several of them has the problem a page of long categories has: the block you want is below the fold because the ones above it are open. Categories have folded since long before widgets existed; a widget could only be dragged, hidden or removed.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetFoldHow: Click a widget's title to fold it shut, or press Enter or Space with the header focused — the same gesture on the same header, rather than a second one to learn. Fold all, the . key and the fold-all button take widgets with them, and each block stays folded or open as you left it, per page.
config.overviewNewFeatureStatsReadingTitle: Statistics reports what the app already knows
config.overviewNewFeatureStatsReadingWhat: The section counted bookmarks, tags and categories and stopped there. It said how many services you monitor but never how well they did, nothing about certificates running out, and nothing about how much of the collection has a saved copy — all of which nextDash had already worked out. Some of what it did report was wrong: the healthy share could read 100% directly above a row saying two monitors were down.
config.overviewNewFeatureStatsReadingHow: Health gains uptime over the last day, week and month with the average response and the outages on record; certificates near expiry, counted per site on your own warning window; and how much of the collection has a copy kept here. Content gains a panel for everything that is not a bookmark — widgets, feeds, import sources, the trash and the automatic backups. The healthy share counts every state now, the cleanup score names the threshold you actually set, category panels show names rather than the ids underneath them, and the timestamp follows your 12- or 24-hour setting.
config.overviewNewFeatureStatsReadingEnable: Nothing to switch on. The uptime and certificate panels appear once there is something to report.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetCatalogueTitle: Adding a widget no longer loses the widget
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetCatalogueWhat: The kinds you can add filled a whole screen at the top of the Widgets tab, which pushed the widgets you already have below the fold. Choosing a kind added something you could not see, and the only sign of it was a message in the opposite corner.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetCatalogueHow: Widgets opens on your own widgets with one button above them. The catalogue opens over the page, the way the theme browser does, and closes onto the new widget with its name ready to type. The Types tab lists every kind with what it does and adds from there too, and the Custom widget comes with twenty-eight services already filled in.
config.tipTuneThemeBrowser: Config → Appearance → Browse opens the theme browser: 107 families as cards you can search and star, each previewing on the real dashboard while you look at it. Nothing is saved until you pick one.
config.tipMaintStatsUptime: Config → Statistics → Health pools uptime across every monitor over the last day, week and month, and lists certificates close to expiry per site — the readings the health view takes one bookmark at a time.
config.tipDataBeyondBookmarks: Config → Statistics → Content counts what is not a bookmark: how many widgets are on your pages and of what kind, your feeds and import sources, what is waiting in the trash, and how many automatic backups are kept.
config.themeDepthNote: How much of the theme is drawn behind the content: the tint in its greys, the raised surfaces, the wash behind the page. Flat is the dashboard as it was before any of it.
config.inkGapNote: How far the fainter text sits from the surface it is drawn on. Every theme is measured against this, so the note beside a bookmark stays readable no matter which palette you pick. Lower gives a softer hierarchy, higher pushes everything toward the foreground.
config.themeBackdropNote: Every theme brings its own backdrop, built from its own colours, so no two look alike. Turn it off for a flat surface. Your own background image, if you set one, is drawn over it either way.
config.backgroundPatternNote: The texture behind the dashboard. Left to the theme, most ask for dots and a few ask for something that suits them. Lines and hatch cover more of the page than dots do, so they read heavier on a light theme.
config.sourceTokenRequired: Paste a token first — this source cannot read anything without one.
config.widgetsDiscardDraftsBody: Your unsaved widget changes on this page will be lost.
config.overviewNewFeatureBrowserHistoryTitle: The browser's Back button moves through nextDash
config.overviewNewFeatureBrowserHistoryWhat: Opening the inbox, health or config, or switching bookmark page, left no trace in the browser's history. Back stripped the address bar and left the view standing, so the URL said one thing and the screen another — and from a view, Back to a bookmarks page did nothing at all.
config.overviewNewFeatureBrowserHistoryHow: Each of those is a history entry now, so Back returns you where you were and Forward brings you back. What counts as a step is deliberately narrow: a filter is not one, so Back leaves the inbox rather than walking through the filters you tried in it, and a config section is not one either, so Back leaves config the way Escape does.
config.overviewNewFeatureBrowserHistoryEnable: Nothing to switch on — it is how the buttons behave now.
config.overviewNewFeatureTriageFinishTitle: A triage run can be finished
config.overviewNewFeatureTriageFinishWhat: The queue held every link the filter showed, including the ones already read, so an inbox of 5 unread and 35 read handed back all forty and asked you to decide again on work already done. The last card looped back to the first rather than ending, and promoting a link closed triage — clearing a backlog of forty meant pressing t forty times.
config.overviewNewFeatureTriageFinishHow: A run now walks the unread only, with the active filter still applying. The last card ends it and says how many you went through. And promoting a link puts you back in the run where you left it, so one t clears the whole backlog.
config.overviewNewFeatureTriageFinishEnable: Press t in the inbox, or use the Triage button above the list.
config.overviewNewFeatureListHeadersTitle: The inbox and health lists start where the rows do
config.overviewNewFeatureListHeadersWhat: Both views put a wall of controls between their heading and their first row: ten bordered summary tiles, a filter strip that scrolled sideways with four filters past its right edge, and eight action buttons across two lines. On a laptop the first bookmark sat below the fold.
config.overviewNewFeatureListHeadersHow: The tiles read as one compact line, the filters wrap so every one of them is on screen, and the actions you rarely use moved behind a ⋯ — Work through and Triage stay where they are. The two views were changed to match each other, so switching between them no longer means learning a second layout.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetTourTitle: A tour of what a custom widget can reach
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetTourWhat: The Custom widget can read any address that answers with JSON, which is the most capable thing in the Widgets section and the hardest to discover: nothing on the page said what it could do or where to start.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetTourHow: Seven steps, opening the first time you visit Config → Widgets. It walks the catalogue of ready-made services, the fields a custom widget maps, and how a figure gets from an endpoint onto your page. Ask for it again from Behavior → General → Onboarding.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetTourEnable: Opens by itself on a first visit to Widgets.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetFigureSizeTitle: Every figure on a custom widget can have its own size
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetFigureSizeWhat: A tile whose numbers were all drawn the same size left you to work out which one mattered. The custom widget drew flat rows where every other tile gave its main figure room, so the number you built the tile for looked exactly like the ones giving it context.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetFigureSizeHow: Each figure is now Normal, Large, Small or a Bar, set per figure when you add or edit it. The bar is offered on a percentage, where a share of a whole is something it can draw, and it takes its colour from the theme you are using.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetFigureSizeEnable: Nothing to switch on — open a custom widget and edit one of its figures.
config.overviewNewFeatureShortcutDisplayTitle: The shortcut letters are on, and have a third setting
config.overviewNewFeatureShortcutDisplayWhat: The shortcut letters were on or off. On, they sat in a column of their own down the right of every category — as loud as the bookmark names beside them, and holding the width that made those names truncate. Off, you lost the reminder of what your own shortcuts are, and some dashboards had lost them years ago without meaning to.
config.overviewNewFeatureShortcutDisplayHow: There is a third answer now: the letter floats in over the end of the name while your pointer or keyboard selection is on that row. Nothing moves when it appears, and the names get about five characters of width back.
config.overviewNewFeatureShortcutDisplayEnable: Config → Appearance → Shortcut letters on rows.
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchNameHintTitle: A search that finds nothing says where to look
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchNameHintWhat: Typing a bookmark's name into the search overlay reported nothing found while the bookmark sat on the page behind it. A plain query looks for a shortcut, not a name, and the overlay never said so.
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchNameHintHow: When there is nothing by that shortcut but something by that name, the overlay adds one line saying how many bookmarks carry it, and Enter runs the search the other way. When nothing matches either, “nothing found” stays the answer.
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchNameHintEnable: Nothing to switch on — it is how search answers now.
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchModeKeyTitle: The search mode has a key of its own
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchModeKeyWhat: Whether typing letters finds a bookmark's name or its shortcut was a tickbox under Appearance → Layout labelled “Interleave categories across columns” — which is not what it does. Nothing about the layout has ever read it, so ticking it to rearrange your columns changed how typing was read and moved nothing on screen.
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchModeKeyHow: It sits under Behavior → Search now, called Switch Search Mode, and Shift + Q flips it from the dashboard itself with a message saying which way it landed — for the times you want the other mode for a single search.
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchModeKeyEnable: Nothing to switch on — Shift + Q works from any bookmark page.
config.overviewNewFeatureChineseWhat: 简体中文 joins English, Dutch, German and French as a fifth full language — and it is the whole of it, not a partial pass. The dashboard and its cheat sheet, the command palette, the setup wizards, every config tab, the statistics, the health view and its reasons, and all 209 headings of the Help tab.
config.overviewNewFeatureChineseHow: Pick it under Appearance → Language. Nothing falls back to English on the way through, and the theme browser — a screen that had stayed English in every language — was translated with it.
config.overviewNewFeatureChineseEnable: Nothing to switch on — choose the language and the whole interface follows.
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchGroupsTitle: Search groups its results, and learns which one you meant
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchGroupsWhat: One letter used to fill the screen. Typing g put Gmail and widGetonderzoek in the same column, in the same style, in an order nothing on screen explained — and the ranking looked the same on your thousandth search as on your first.
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchGroupsHow: Results now group by why they matched: the strong ones stay open, the rest fold behind a heading and a count, and nothing is thrown away. The ranking reads how often you open a bookmark and remembers which result you picked for the keystrokes you picked it with, so mail can become your own alias for Gmail without a shortcut for it.
config.overviewNewFeatureSearchGroupsEnable: Nothing to switch on — open the search and type.
config.clearPreviewImagesConfirm: Remove every cached preview image? They are fetched again when next needed.
config.clearPreviewImagesError: Could not remove the cached images.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewMediaWhat: Hovering a bookmark asked that website for its picture directly, so the site learned you were looking at your own dashboard — and a site that refuses to hand its picture to anyone else left the card blank. On a real collection that was every picture leaking and two of sixteen cards empty.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewMediaHow: nextDash fetches the picture and the site's icon once and keeps them, so hovering reaches nothing but your own dashboard. The card opens with its text straight away and the picture lands on the card you already have open — it never waits on someone else's server.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewMediaEnable: Nothing to switch on — and you can switch it off: untick Image in the card's row checklist under Appearance → Display, and nothing is drawn, fetched or stored. Icons & previews shows what is kept and can remove it.
config.statsGrowthPartial: Counted from the {dated} of {total} bookmarks that carry a date. Older ones were saved before nextDash recorded it.
config.overviewNewFeatureSystemWidgetsTitle: Four widgets that watch the machine
config.overviewNewFeatureSystemWidgetsWhat: A dashboard that knew everything about your links knew nothing about the machine serving them — whether the disk was filling up, whether a container had quietly stopped.
config.overviewNewFeatureSystemWidgetsHow: Processor, Memory, Disks and Containers report on the host itself. Memory counts the file cache as the spare room it is, so a healthy machine stops looking full. On Docker they need read-only mounts you opt into; without one the tile says so and names the step rather than showing a plausible wrong number.
config.overviewNewFeatureSystemWidgetsEnable: Add them under Widgets. Config → Help and the README carry the mounts, including the Unraid template rows.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetsTabTitle: The Widgets tab works like Bookmarks
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetsTabWhat: A page with a dozen widgets was a single column to scroll, with no way to find one by name and no way to act on more than one at a time.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetsTabHow: The same toolbar you already know: a search across names and types, a page picker and a sort, grouped by default. All pages shows every page’s widgets at once, and ticking several lets you show, hide, move or delete them together.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetsTabEnable: Nothing to switch on — it is how the tab works now.
config.overviewNewFeatureReviewSnoozeTitle: Put the review card away for a month
config.overviewNewFeatureReviewSnoozeWhat: The card offering ten links to review had one way out, Not today, which comes back tomorrow. For someone not doing maintenance this month that is the pattern people learn to ignore.
config.overviewNewFeatureReviewSnoozeHow: Remind me in 30 days puts it away properly, and it returns on its own. It touches no bookmark: this is about the invitation, not about what health reports.
config.overviewNewFeatureReviewSnoozeEnable: On the card itself, beside Not today.
config.overviewNewFeatureFinderFallbackTitle: A search that finds nothing offers your finders
config.overviewNewFeatureFinderFallbackWhat: Searching for something that is not in your dashboard ended there: a line saying nothing matched, and no way onward without retyping the same words somewhere else.
config.overviewNewFeatureFinderFallbackHow: The finders you use most now sit under that line, carrying the words you already typed. Click one, or arrow down and press Enter. Brave Search comes with nextDash on ?B — and if you had already added Brave yourself, yours is left exactly as you set it up.
config.overviewNewFeatureFinderFallbackEnable: On by default. Include finders in search, under Behavior → Search, switches it off.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeShortcutWhat: Trying a different theme meant leaving what you were doing: into config, into Appearance, then into the browser.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeShortcutHow: Shift+A opens it over whatever is on screen — all of your themes, searchable, previewing on the real dashboard as you move across them. Escape closes it and leaves the theme you had.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeShortcutEnable: Nothing to switch on. Press ! or F1 for the full list of shortcuts.
config.overviewNewFeatureStatsFiguresTitle: Statistics shows what the install already knew
config.overviewNewFeatureStatsFiguresWhat: Four things were recorded and never shown: how many bookmarks are pinned, when anything was last edited, when a page was last kept as a copy, and how long the longest-standing broken link has been failing. “1 broken” never said whether that was yesterday or March.
config.overviewNewFeatureStatsFiguresHow: All four are on the Statistics section now, and a new panel counts what you added per month — saying how many bookmarks carry a date, so anything saved before nextDash recorded one is left out rather than quietly folded in.
config.widgetAbout.cpu: How hard the processor is working, and whether work is queueing up behind it.
config.widgetAbout.weather: Current conditions beside a forecast, for the location the header already reads.
config.widgetAbout.calendar: What is coming up, from the ICS feed set in Behavior → Date & weather.
config.widgetCpuRefreshHint: One second is the fastest useful reading: below that the figure is noise.
config.widgetCpuSetupLead: This reads the machine, not the container. /proc/stat is not namespaced, so a container already counts the host’s processor — even one started with a CPU limit, because that limit lives in cgroups, which this does not read.
config.widgetCpuSetupTail: So on a NAS or a Linux server nothing needs adding, and the mount below only makes explicit which /proc is read — on Unraid, one Path row (/proc to /host/proc, Read Only) and one Variable row. On Docker Desktop for Mac or Windows the figures come from its Linux VM; it is usually given every core, so the processor reads true even there. Running the binary directly needs nothing at all.
config.widgetAbout.disks: How full each disk is, and how much room is actually left on it.
config.widgetDisksRefreshHint: Free space moves slowly, and reading a sleeping disk can stall.
config.widgetDisksMountsHint: Paths as this machine knows them — on Unraid /mnt/user and /mnt/cache, on a NAS /volume1.
config.widgetDisksLabelsHint: Written as path=name, so /mnt/user=Files. Without one a disk shows its path.
config.widgetDisksInodesToggle: Show how full the file table is
config.widgetDisksSetupLead: Running nextDash in Docker? A container can only measure what is mounted into it, so add the disks you want to watch and point NEXTDASH_HOST_ROOT at them, then recreate the container.
config.widgetDisksSetupTail: Then name the disks above as this machine knows them — /mnt/user, /mnt/cache — not as the container sees them. On Unraid that is one Path row (/mnt to /host/root/mnt, Read Only) and one Variable row in the container template; mount / to /host/root instead to reach disks outside the array. Running the binary directly needs nothing.
config.widgetDisksNoneFound: No disks found to offer — type a path, or check the mount above.
config.widgetAbout.memory: How much memory is really in use, with the file cache counted as the spare room it is.
config.widgetMemoryCacheHint: Memory the machine is keeping warm and will hand back the moment anything needs it.
config.widgetMemorySetupLead: This reads the machine, not the container. /proc/meminfo is not namespaced, so a container sees the whole host — even one started with a memory limit reports the full amount, because that limit lives in cgroups, which this does not read.
config.widgetMemorySetupTail: So on a NAS or a Linux server nothing needs adding, and the mount below only makes explicit which /proc is read. On Docker Desktop for Mac or Windows the figures are its Linux VM, not your computer — a 24 GB laptop shows the VM’s 8 GB, and no mount changes that, because the VM cannot see the memory outside it. On Unraid, one Path row (/proc to /host/proc, Read Only) and one Variable row.
config.widgetAbout.docker: How many containers run, how many do not, and which have a failing healthcheck.
config.widgetDockerNamesHint: A count sends you looking; a name does not.
config.widgetDockerRestartedHint: Up for minutes while the rest have run for days — the shape of a crashloop.
config.widgetDockerSetupLead: This one needs the Docker socket, and that is a real grant: read-only still exposes the daemon’s whole read API — every container, its image, its environment, its mounts. Add it only if you are content with that for a container count.
config.widgetDockerSetupTail: On Unraid that is one Path row (/var/run/docker.sock, Read Only) and one Variable row. Docker Desktop keeps its socket elsewhere — run "docker context ls" to find it. If the grant is more than you want, put a socket proxy in front and point this at that instead.
config.widgetResetAria: Reset this widget to its defaults
config.widgetResetNotice: Settings back to their defaults — Save to keep this.
config.widgetDockerShowInfoBody:
Tick the ones you want on the tile. Leave them all unticked and you get every figure — which also means a figure added in a later version appears on its own, rather than staying hidden because you once saved this panel.

The tile always leads with running against total, whatever you pick here: that pairing is what makes the number mean something.
config.widgetMemoryCacheInfoBody:
Linux keeps recently read files in spare memory. It is handed straight back the moment a program needs it, so it is free memory doing something useful in the meantime.

This is why the tile shows a low figure where other tools show a machine that looks nearly full: in use here counts what cannot be handed back, and the cache is listed separately rather than folded in.
config.widgetDisksMountsInfoBody:
Write the paths as this machine knows them — /mnt/user, /mnt/cache, /volume1 — not as the container sees them. The server translates between the two.

They are named rather than found automatically because a container sees dozens of mounts that are nothing to do with your storage. Whatever is mounted and readable is offered under the field.
config.widgetRefreshInfoBody:
How many seconds between readings. Leave it empty for the default.

Each kind has a floor, because below it the reading stops meaning anything: a processor figure is the difference between two samples, so a fraction of a second is measurement noise rather than a measurement. Free space has a higher floor still, since reading a sleeping disk can stall.

A hidden browser tab asks for nothing at all, whatever this says.
config.widgetsBulkDeleteBody: Remove {n} widgets? Their settings and any sign-ins they hold go with them.
config.widgetsMoveFailed: Could not read the other page — nothing was moved.
config.helpWidgetSystemTitle: The system widgets, and the mounts they need
config.helpWidgetSystemBody:
Four widgets — Processor, Memory, Disks and Containers — report on the machine nextDash runs on rather than on your bookmarks. They are the only ones that need anything set up, because a container cannot see the machine around it unless you let it.

Processor and Memory usually need nothing. /proc is not namespaced, so a container already reads the host's processor and memory — even one started with a CPU or memory limit, because that limit lives in cgroups, which these do not read. Mount /proc at /host/proc and set NEXTDASH_HOST_PROC only to be explicit about which one is read.

Disks do need a mount. A container can only measure filesystems mounted into it: without one it reports its own overlay — under a gigabyte — instead of your array. Mount the disks you want to watch under a prefix, keeping their own names, and point NEXTDASH_HOST_ROOT at that prefix:

volumes:
  - /mnt:/host/root/mnt:ro,rslave
environment:
  - NEXTDASH_HOST_ROOT=/host/root

Then name the disks in the widget's settings as this machine knows them — /mnt/user, /mnt/cache, /volume1 — never as the container sees them; the server translates between the two. Whatever is mounted and readable is offered under the field, so you can click rather than type. They are named rather than found automatically because a container sees dozens of mounts that have nothing to do with your storage.

Containers need the Docker socket, and that is a real grant. Read-only still exposes the daemon's whole read API: every container, its image, its environment, its mounts. Add it only if you are content with that for a container count — and if you are not, put a socket proxy in front and point nextDash at that instead.

volumes:
  - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
environment:
  - NEXTDASH_DOCKER_SOCKET=/var/run/docker.sock

Docker Desktop keeps its socket elsewhere; docker context ls names the path.

On Unraid these are rows in the container template rather than compose lines. Each mount is one Path row with Access Mode Read Only, and each variable is one Variable row. For the array that is Container Path /host/root/mnt, Host Path /mnt, plus NEXTDASH_HOST_ROOT=/host/root — then name /mnt/user and /mnt/cache in the widget. Mount / to /host/root instead to reach disks outside the array. A user share reports the pool total, which is the figure Unraid's own dashboard shows.

Running the binary directly needs none of this — /proc and your disks are already the host's.

Nothing is guessed. A source that is not mounted says so on the tile and names the step, rather than showing a plausible wrong number. The processor figure stays blank until a second sample exists, because a percentage is the difference between two readings. Each widget sets its own refresh interval, each has a floor below which the reading stops meaning anything, and a hidden browser tab asks for nothing at all.

One caveat worth knowing: on Docker Desktop for Mac or Windows the figures describe its Linux VM rather than your computer. A laptop with 24 GB shows the VM's 8, and no mount changes that, because the VM cannot see the memory outside it. On a NAS or Linux server there is no VM in between and the figures are the machine's own.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthRailTitle: Health reads like the Inbox now
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthRailWhat: A row of tiles sat above the list with the same counts the filter pills carried underneath them, so the same numbers were on screen twice and the list started halfway down the page.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthRailHow: Every filter is a row in a left column with its count beside it, and Score, the trend, the broken count and the report's age sit above them as plain readouts. A filter with nothing in it drops out and comes back when it fills. The header stays with you as you scroll, so Work through and the Rot report are reachable from anywhere in a long list.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthRailEnable: Nothing to switch on. Rows follow the compact or comfortable setting the Inbox already reads.
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitorsPlaceTitle: All monitors is a place, not a filter
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitorsPlaceWhat: Monitored narrowed the list to the bookmarks you watch, while the fleet readouts — pooled uptime, the worst performers, recent outages — were a panel you had to find.
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitorsPlaceHow: All monitors is its own row in the left column and swaps the list for the fleet panel. It has its own address, so you can bookmark it and come back to the same screen; picking a filter leaves it and goes back to the list.
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitorsPlaceEnable: It appears as soon as there is anything to monitor.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxRailTitle: The inbox has a left column
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxRailWhat: Four tiles above the list repeated the counts already on the filters below them, and the header scrolled away with Triage on it.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxRailHow: The filters moved into a left column with their counts, This week sits above them as a plain readout, and Snoozed and With note appear only when there is something in them. The header stays put and shrinks to a single bar. On a phone the column becomes one scrolling line, so a narrow screen gets the list instead of rows of controls.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxRailEnable: Nothing to switch on. Rows can be compact or comfortable, one setting for the whole app.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeCharacterTitle: A theme can be more than a palette
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeCharacterWhat: A theme was thirteen flat colours, which is why 214 of them could look like one theme in 214 tints: two themes could differ in hue and in nothing else — not in shape, not in weight, not in whether their surfaces were solid.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeCharacterHow: A theme can now say how solid its raised surfaces are, how much they blur and glow, how round the corners sit, and how the category labels are set. Glass joins Flat, Soft and Rich as a depth. Every existing theme renders exactly as it did — leaving a setting out means today's behaviour.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeCharacterEnable: Appearance → Theme, under Depth and backdrop.
config.overviewNewFeatureDerivedInkTitle: The faint text follows the surface it sits on
config.overviewNewFeatureDerivedInkWhat: A theme picks its three text colours against the page and then never adjusts them, while the surfaces rise above it. Every layer costs contrast that nobody sees coming, because measured against the page each theme is fine — across the 107 dark built-ins, tertiary text was under 3.0:1 on a third of them.
config.overviewNewFeatureDerivedInkHow: Secondary and tertiary text are now derived from the surface underneath them, so they hold their distance wherever they land. Every shipped theme clears the 4.5:1 floor for body text, and a test measures the whole register so a new theme that lands under it says so first.
config.overviewNewFeatureDerivedInkEnable: Nothing to switch on. The step between ink and surface is yours to move under Appearance.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthInboxShellTitle: Health and the Inbox share one left rail
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthInboxShellWhat: Health and the inbox each carried a row of tiles above the list, repeating the same counts the filters below already showed — the same number, twice, in two different shapes.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthInboxShellHow: Both now list every filter in a left column with its count instead. Score, the trend, the broken count and the report's age sit above Health's filters as plain readouts; This week sits the same way above the inbox's. A filter with nothing in it drops out of the list and returns once it fills, and both headers now stay put while you scroll, so the filters and the actions above the list stay reachable in a long one.
config.overviewNewFeatureWeatherWidgetTitle: A weather block for your page
config.overviewNewFeatureWeatherWidgetWhat: The header could show one line of weather, and that was all a dashboard knew about the sky: today's temperature, with no idea whether tomorrow is worth planning around.
config.overviewNewFeatureWeatherWidgetHow: A Weather widget puts the conditions now beside a forecast — three days, five days, or the next 24 hours, whichever you pick per block. It reads the location, source and unit you already set for the header line, so there is nothing to fill in twice, and it refreshes itself while the page is open.
config.overviewNewFeatureWeatherWidgetEnable: Config → Widgets → Add a widget → Weather. Set the location first under Behavior → Date & weather.
config.overviewNewFeatureCalendarWidgetTitle: What is coming up, on the dashboard
config.overviewNewFeatureCalendarWidgetWhat: Your dashboard is the first page of the day, and it could point at your calendar but never show it — what was on today lived in another tab.
config.overviewNewFeatureCalendarWidgetHow: A Calendar widget lists what is coming up from your own calendar. Paste the sharing address your calendar app gives you once, and every calendar block reads it, each with its own look-ahead in days and its own number of rows. A repeating appointment shows the date it names rather than every repeat.
config.overviewNewFeatureCalendarWidgetEnable: Behavior → Date & weather → Calendar feed URL, then Config → Widgets → Add a widget → Calendar.
config.overviewNewFeatureLockLayoutTitle: Lock a layout you are happy with
config.overviewNewFeatureLockLayoutWhat: Bookmarks and categories move by dragging, which is what you want while you arrange a page and not what you want afterwards — one stray drag on a tidy page and something is somewhere else.
config.overviewNewFeatureLockLayoutHow: Lock layout switches dragging off for both bookmarks and categories. Sorting, adding, renaming and deleting carry on exactly as before; only the drag gesture stops, and the page says so when you try.
config.overviewNewFeatureLockLayoutEnable: Behavior → General → Lock layout, or type :lock-layout.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthMonitorsTitle: Monitors is a place of its own
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthMonitorsWhat: The Monitored filter narrows the list to what could be watched, but the pooled uptime, the worst performers and recent outages used to live under that same filter — one control asked to do two different things.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthMonitorsHow: Monitors is now its own entry in the rail. Opening it swaps the list for that fleet panel instead of narrowing it, and it has its own address, so it is bookmarkable and returns you to the same view on reload.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthMonitorsEnable: Appears in the rail as soon as anything on the page could be monitored.
config.overviewNewFeatureListDensityTitle: Rows can sit closer together or further apart
config.overviewNewFeatureListDensityWhat: Health and the inbox always drew rows at the same height, whether you wanted to scan a long list quickly or read one comfortably.
config.overviewNewFeatureListDensityHow: A density setting switches every list between compact and comfortable rows. It is one setting for the whole app rather than one per view, so switching it from either the inbox or Health changes both.
config.overviewNewFeatureListDensityEnable: Two buttons in the header of Health and the inbox.
